name: en-multi-topic

messages.content: Two things today. First: what's the actual difference between Docker bridge and host networking?

Bridge mode gives the container its own network namespace with a virtual interface on the docker0 bridge; containers reach the host via the gateway IP and publish ports explicitly. Host mode skips namespacing entirely: the container shares the host network stack, so no port publishing and lower overhead, but no isolation.
Makes sense. Unrelated: our CI pipeline is slow because every job re-downloads Go modules. How do people cache that?

Cache the module directory keyed by go.sum's hash. In GitHub Actions that's actions/cache on ~/go/pkg/mod with key ${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}. Restore before go build and you skip the downloads on cache hits.
Back to docker — if I use bridge mode, how do two containers talk to each other?

Put them on the same user-defined bridge network (docker network create, then --network on both). They resolve each other by container name via the built-in DNS; the default bridge doesn't give you name resolution.
And for CI, does the build cache itself need separate handling from the module cache?

Yes, cache the build cache separately: for Go that's ~/.cache/go-build, also keyed by go.sum plus optionally the toolchain version. Modules change rarely; the build cache changes every commit, so keep them as two cache entries.
